column1: # Skill description manifest — curated frontmatter for SKILL.md generation
# - Lines starting with # and blank lines are ignored.
# - <skill-name> must be lowercase letters/digits/hyphens (Claude Code skill-name rule).
# - mendix/* skills are prefixed `mendix-` to avoid clashes with top-level dev skills.
# - <description> is the discovery trigger Claude reads to decide whether to load the skill.
#   Keep it third-person and lead with "Use when…".
# Regenerate the SKILL.md tree with:  tools/generate-skillmd.sh

column3: Use when debugging BSON serialization errors while programmatically creating Mendix pages and widgets — Studio Pro crashes such as "Sequence contains no matching element" at MprObject/MprProperty, or CE0463 widget-definition errors. Systematic diff workflow using the mx tool.

Use before designing new MDL syntax — grammar rules, AST types, or executor code for a new document type, microflow action, or operation. Covers design guardrails, standard verb patterns, and anti-patterns.
Use when diagnosing and fixing a bug in mxcli itself. Fast-path symptom-to-file table that routes you to the right layer before opening files.
Use when implementing a new MDL feature end-to-end — a new Mendix action type, page widget, or document type — across grammar, AST, visitor, executor, and backend.
Use when hand-building SVG diagrams rendered in the VS Code extension webviews (ELK system overview or any new SVG). Enforces the sketch / proof-of-concept visual style.
Use when testing MDL scripts against the ModelSDK Go implementation and verifying they open correctly in Studio Pro, especially after adding BSON serialization for a new document type.
Use when sending MDL commands to a running mxcli TUI over its Unix socket so agent actions simulate visible, interruptible user operations.
Use before generating any MDL — check the project's Mendix version (show features) so you never emit syntax the project cannot support. Read first for version-gated features.
Use when implementing new MDL commands that read from or write to MPR files — full stack from grammar to BSON serialization, including storage-name gotchas.
Use when creating or managing Mendix AI Agent documents (Agent, Model, Knowledge Base, Consumed MCP Service) stored as JSON in the MPR. Requires AgentEditorCommons, Mendix 11.9+.
Use when modifying an existing page or snippet's widget tree in-place with ALTER PAGE / ALTER SNIPPET (SET, INSERT, DROP, REPLACE) instead of recreating it.
Use when investigating an existing non-Mendix application to produce a structured assessment for migrating it to Mendix.
Use when performing a comprehensive quality assessment of a Mendix project against best practices (naming, security, performance, maintainability, architecture).
Use when discovering external services and querying integration assets via the MDL CATALOG keyword (SELECT ... FROM CATALOG.*). Not the external Mendix Catalog CLI.
Use when discovering and bulk-editing widget properties across many pages/snippets with show widgets / update widgets (experimental; dry run first).
Use when defining event-driven APIs with business events over Kafka or message brokers (SHOW/DESCRIBE/CREATE/DROP).
Use when searching the external Mendix Catalog service registry (catalog.mendix.com via mxcli catalog search). Requires platform auth. Not the MDL CATALOG keyword.
Use when debugging common MDL syntax errors — quick symptom-to-fix lookups for variable, entity, and association mistakes.
Use when declaring variables in MDL microflows or fixing variable-declaration errors — quick syntax reference.
Use before presenting or executing any MDL script — pre-flight validation checklist with mxcli check (and --references).
Use when fetching data from a RapidMiner graph mart or any SPARQL 1.1 HTTP endpoint (e.g. AnzoGraph) and surfacing it in a Mendix app.
Use when building a Mendix pluggable widget from scratch with React + TypeScript, producing a .mpk for Studio Pro.
Use when writing CREATE PAGE statements — page and widget MDL syntax reference.
Use when writing MDL for GALLERY, COMBOBOX, DataGrid2, or other built-in/third-party pluggable widgets in CREATE PAGE / ALTER PAGE, including child slots and adding new widgets via .def.json.
Use when setting up external database connections (Oracle, PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQL Server) via the Mendix External Database Connector and mapping SQL results to non-persistent entities.
Use when debugging BSON serialization issues while implementing or fixing Mendix SDK writers.
Use for any database/import or demo-data work — connect to the Mendix app's PostgreSQL directly, understand the Mendix ID system and association storage, and seed data.
Use when building, running, and testing a Mendix app with Docker inside a devcontainer.
Use when defining and reusing widget groups across pages with 'define fragment'.
Use when generating a full Mendix domain model (entities, attributes, associations, enumerations) in MDL and validating it with the linter.
Use when creating or calling custom Java actions in Mendix projects via MDL.
Use when adding, updating, or removing Maven/JAR dependencies for a Mendix module (Studio Pro Module Settings → Java dependencies).
Use when creating or describing JSON structures, import mappings, and export mappings in MDL, and mapping JSON to entities.
Use when inspecting or modifying navigation profiles — home pages, menu items, login pages, role-based routing.
Use when configuring Mendix security via MDL — module/user roles, access rules (microflows, pages, entities), project security settings, demo users, GRANT/REVOKE.
Use when building master-detail page layouts (selectable master list plus detail panel).
Use when creating entities, attributes, and associations — complete entity/attribute/association MDL syntax reference.
Use when assessing or migrating K2 / Nintex K2 applications to Mendix with MDL.
Use when assessing or migrating Oracle Forms applications to Mendix with MDL.
Use when sharing data between Mendix apps via OData services, using view entities to decouple the API contract from the domain model.
Use when organizing project documents into folders or moving pages/microflows/snippets between folders and modules (MOVE command).
Use when building standard CRUD overview and edit pages (list/grid pattern with navigation snippet).
Use when implementing Create/Read/Update/Delete microflow logic — standard CRUD action patterns and naming conventions.
Use when processing lists of data — loops, aggregates, batch processing, delta merge, and list-operation patterns. Read before writing list-processing microflows.
Use when configuring project settings — database connections, constants, runtime settings (SHOW/DESCRIBE/ALTER).
Use when an MDL script fails because it references a document created later in the same script — ordering and forward-reference resolution.
Use when generating the full REST integration stack from a JSON payload — JSON Structure → entities → import mapping → microflow (inline REST CALL approach).
Use when integrating with external REST APIs from Mendix microflows — covers the three calling approaches.
Use when building and starting the Mendix app in Docker.
Use when calling the Mendix M2EE runtime admin API (port 8090) directly, for example with curl.
Use when referencing built-in Mendix System module entities (users, files, workflows, task queues, HTTP) in microflows, pages, associations, or Java actions.
Use when verifying a running Mendix app end-to-end with playwright-cli browser automation and mxcli oql data assertions.
Use for testing work — writing and running MDL-based microflow tests with mxcli test (.test.mdl/.test.md; requires Docker).
Use when working with SCSS theming — custom-variables.scss, themesource/ directories, SCSS compilation and caveats.
Use when creating validation microflows that validate user input on NewEdit pages and return feedback.
Use when verifying microflow side effects and data changes with OQL queries against a running Mendix app.
Use when writing custom Starlark lint rules (.star) in .claude/lint-rules/ that run with mxcli lint.
Use before writing any microflow — comprehensive microflow MDL syntax, common mistakes, and validation checklist.
Use before writing any nanoflow — client-side nanoflow MDL syntax, restrictions, disallowed activities, and validation checklist.
Use when creating VIEW entities — correct OQL query syntax that executes in the Mendix runtime.
Use when writing XPath constraint expressions in RETRIEVE WHERE clauses, page data sources, or security rules — association paths, nested predicates, functions.
